title: User guide for Daphnia microinjection
author: Sam Paplauskas
materials: Design your construct, guide RNAs, or primers (~1–2 weeks before injection): Synthesis of guide RNA (gRNA): Determine the target gene (or region) for genome editing. Design gRNA sites for the target gene using CRISPR direct : https://crispr.dbcls.jp/ (see Fig. 5). Figure 5. Design of gRNA sites using CRIPSR direct. Synthesize gRNA using the Precision gRNA Synthesis Kit : https://www.thermofisher.com/order/catalog/product/jp/ja/A29377 Store at -80 °C .

Reagent preparation (~3–7 days before injection): Mix Cas9 protein and gRNA with final concentrations of 600 ng/µL and 500 ng/µL , respectively, using fluorescent dye (Alexa 488) for dilution. Store the RNPs at -80 °C . Cas9 protein: TrueCut Cas9 Protein v2 https://www.thermofisher.com/order/catalog/product/A36498 Alexa 488 dye: https://www.thermofisher.com/jp/ja/home/life-science/cell-analysis/fluorophores/alexa-fluor-488.html

Final prep / injection-ready (1 day before or same day): Note: Final concentrations depend on clone ( D. pulex or D. magna ) Dilute reagent to working concentration. Prepare Injection Buffer (M4-Sucrose) o Prepare 120 mM Sucrose Solution § MilliQ water: 1 L § Sucrose: 41.4 g → Store in the refrigerator after preparation. o Prepare M4 Solution → Store in therefrigerator after preparation. o Prepare M4-Sucrose Solution § Mix 120 mM sucrose solution and M4 solution in a 1:1 ratio , while filter sterilizing . The resulting M4 solution containing 60 mM sucrose should be stored in the refrigerator. § Filter: MF-Millipore Membrane (Mixed Cellulose Esters)

steps.title: Prepare Daphnia Stock
steps.instruction: Prepare a population of highly fecund Daphnia approximately 2–3 weeks before the injection experiment.

substeps.instruction: Transfer individuals into a new environment with favorable growth conditions.
Maintain a secondary 'mini-stock' to replenish the experimental population after sampling.
Ensure a population size sufficient to sample ~20 Daphnia per attempt.

steps.title: Collect and Screen Samples
steps.instruction: Select and collect females about to lay eggs using a stereomicroscope.

substeps.instruction: Identify females with the following characteristics: embryo development stage 5 (single black eye), fully developed green ovaries, and a darkened carapace (indicating next molting shell formation).
Collect ~20 Daphnia and move them to a 48-well plate, placing one individual and some media in each well.

steps.title: Prepare Reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare the injection reagents while maintaining cold temperatures.

substeps.instruction: Prepare ice in advance.
Retrieve Cas9–gRNA reagent stock from -80 °C and thaw on ice.
Gently mix by pipetting and briefly spin down to collect contents; do not vortex.
Determine the required working volume.

steps.title: Set Up Dissection and Injection Workspace
steps.instruction: Organize the core setup and injection working space for maximum efficiency.

substeps.instruction: Prepare an ice box containing injection buffer (~50 mL in a Falcon tube), a dissection well plate (kept on ice), and a petri dish for injection.

Gather tools: stopwatch, small jar with extra media, cover slide, 5 mL pipette (intact tip for removing media), 5 mL pipette (cut tip for transferring adults), dissecting tweezers, cover slip, P20 micropipette with slightly cut tips, 35 mm petri dish with normal media, scissors, and a light pad.
Set up the injection station with a micropipette (e.g., P2), microloader tips, pulled needles, a Falcon tube for used needles, and a fluorescence observation setup if required.

steps.title: Configure Injection Machine and Micromanipulator
steps.instruction: Power on and calibrate the microinjection system and micromanipulator.

substeps.instruction: Turn on the injection system, ensuring pressure/air tubing is securely connected.
Allow the system to complete automatic pressure calibration.
Set injection parameters (pressure, injection time, compensation pressure) based on species (D. pulex or D. magna) and needle type.
Select the correct capillary/needle settings from the menu.
Position the micromanipulator, secure the needle holder, and zero/calibrate the axes.

steps.title: Prepare and Load Needle
steps.instruction: Mount, inspect, and load the glass needle with the reagent.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve a pulled glass needle and mount it onto the micromanipulator.
Inspect under the microscope to ensure the tip is straight, sharp, and not bent.
Align the needle at a shallow angle (~20–40° relative to the dish surface).
Use a microloader tip to inject 5–10 μL of sample into the blunt end of the capillary.
Eject the sample while slowly withdrawing the loading tip to avoid air bubbles; tap the needle to dislodge any bubbles.
Briefly apply pressure to confirm the reagent reaches the needle tip.

steps.title: Dissect and Collect Embryos
steps.instruction: Monitor Daphnia for oviposition and collect embryos immediately after laying.

substeps.instruction: Check for molting every 30 minutes (keep on light pad with light off); check individuals every 10 minutes once molting occurs.
Transfer Daphnia into an embryo dish containing M4-Sucrose cooled on ice once oviposition begins.
Start the stopwatch after egg-laying finishes (when eggs are round or 80% complete).
Immobilize the organism by applying gentle pressure to the dorsal region (heart) or securing appendages with fine forceps.
Open the carapace along the dorsal side and remove embryos using a pipette, or tear the carapace and agitate the specimen in a droplet of medium.

steps.title: Set Up Injection Dish
steps.instruction: Prepare the microscope and dish for the injection process.

substeps.instruction: Place a petri dish under the stereomicroscope and add injection buffer (e.g., M4).
Submerge a clean cover slip and position it against the edge of the dish to stabilize embryos.
Prepare a separate 35 mm petri dish with standard media for post-injection transfer.

steps.title: Perform Microinjection
steps.instruction: Inject the embryos using precise positioning and needle control.

substeps.instruction: Verify reagent flow (should look like a colorless puff of air) before injecting.
Position the embryo so its longest side is parallel to the cover slide and it is in direct contact with the slide to prevent movement.
Focus the microscope so that the embryo and ONLY the tip of the needle are in focus (the needle body should be out of focus).
Center the needle tip in the middle of the embryo to avoid bursting the membrane.
Apply gentle, controlled pressure using the foot pedal.
Penetrate the embryo to a depth of approximately 1/3 of the embryo width.
Immediately separate injected embryos using a micropipette into individually labeled Petri dishes containing media.

steps.title: Maintain Needle Between Attempts
steps.instruction: Clean and reposition for subsequent injections.

substeps.instruction: Flush the injection needle between attempts to prevent clogging.
Gently move the petri dish to bring the next embryo into the field of view to avoid repeated pipette repositioning.

steps.title: Verify Injection Success
steps.instruction: Assess the success of the injection using fluorescence microscopy.

substeps.instruction: Wait approximately 120 minutes for embryo membranes to harden before handling.
In a dark room, use a fluorescence microscope with the appropriate filter, avoiding long/intense light exposure.
Confirm that fluorescence is evenly distributed throughout the cells (small spots indicate unsuccessful penetration).
If fluorescence is absent, test a small volume of stock dye on a slide as a control to rule out dye degradation.

steps.title: Shut Down Equipment
steps.instruction: Properly power off the injection machine.

substeps.instruction: Press and hold the off switch while the pressure releases (listen for the release noise) to avoid damaging the machine.

steps.title: Incubate and Analyze Phenotype
steps.instruction: Culture the injected embryos and screen for heritable modifications.

substeps.instruction: Incubate embryos under normal conditions, replacing fresh media every 1-2 days and applying antibiotics (optionally use agar to increase survival).
Monitor development and survival to the juvenile stage, then transfer individuals to larger containers.
Visually assess phenotype changes under a microscope in the second generation to quantify heritability and mosaic expression.
